solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cellar barrels' opening gets troops in a fix

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so take the start of barrels
in says the soldiers' word is placed within the a-plus-fix piece

parts.note: to fix something is to set it
troops are men

explanation.surface: Barrels being opened while soldiers find themselves in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is the underground storey of a house, a synonym of the lowest floor below ground.

clue.text: Escape in the Old Railway Inn

indicators.note: in puts the leaking word inside the railway abbreviation

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway of Great Britain
to ooze is to escape slowly, as liquid does

explanation.surface: A getaway set in a pub called the Old Railway Inn.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stands for British Rail, the UK's state railway until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A boozer is British slang for a pub, the everyday sense of an inn.

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of baby are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A noisy infant is told to hush because it is grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby means worn and grubby, so it can stand for scruffy or soiled.

indicators.note: breaks says the daughter letter splits the dinner word open

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: A daughter interrupts the household as the dinner gong sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for an honour or award such as a military decoration.

clue.text: More stylish Northern Ireland newspaper? That's right

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Belfast paper is smarter and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty means smart or stylish, so its comparative means more stylish.

clue.text: Showbiz columnist's worst gripes erupting about paparazzi ultimately

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the final letter of paparazzi
erupting suggests the letters of worst gripes bursting out into a new arrangement
ultimately points to the last letter of the word paparazzi

explanation.surface: A celebrity journalist's complaints boil over about the photographers who hound stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupting' rearranges WORSTGRIPES around I, the last letter of paparazzi.
explanation.definitionFit: A columnist covering showbusiness tittle-tattle is a classic Fleet Street role, the scandal hack of the papers.

clue.text: Rowdy using horn approaching at speed

indicators.note: rowdy suggests disorder, so the letters of using horn are thrown about

explanation.surface: A boisterous driver blaring the horn as they bear down quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Onrushing describes something surging forward fast towards you.

parts.note: sat, past tense of sit, means settled down
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A student complains that the agreed tuition fee is too high.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it thoroughly, a synonym for drench.

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the clergyman piece sits inside

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself, intrinsically

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so the reverend's abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A stubborn clergyman who has stepped down still amuses people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' means turned back, so the clergyman's abbreviation is reversed; 'entertaining' puts it inside the Latin phrase for intrinsically.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse behaviour is deliberately contrary, the same stubbornness as being bloody-minded.

parts.note: on can mean about or regarding
to doff a hat or coat is to shed it

explanation.surface: Talk about a newly built garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening intermittently, stopping and starting, occurs fitfully.

clue.text: Oxford perhaps in need of articulation? Get away!

indicators.note: articulation means saying it out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Oxford needs better speech, then tells a pest to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university or city, but it is the lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is the exclamation used to drive away animals or people.

clue.text: Decorate half of them rather like Big Ben?

indicators.note: half of takes two of the four letters of them, here the back pair

parts.note: Big Ben is the great bell in London's Westminster clock tower, so something rather like it is bell-ish

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make half of the items resemble the famous London clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is strictly the bell, not the tower, which is why the comparison yields BELLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish is to adorn or ornament, a synonym of decorate.

definitions.meaning: stuff is an old word for woven cloth; this is a twilled worsted fabric
a common French man's first name, as in Gainsbourg

explanation.surface: An angry cry to dismiss a man from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a durable twilled fabric, and also a typical French given name.

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for a dock is heard rather than read

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage or dock

explanation.surface: A man stands trial in the dock, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like the courtroom dock, but it is a quay.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is an equal or fellow, someone of the same standing.

indicators.note: giving coverage means the journalist's letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: ed, an editor, is the crossword journalist
strange means unusual

explanation.surface: A disgruntled reporter whose news reporting takes an odd slant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone estranged has become alienated or no longer friendly, hence disaffected.

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of it's a Poe are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a book titled Narcotics was written by Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it is the anagram signal; Poe famously used laudanum.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are drugs derived from opium, the classic narcotics.

clue.text: Greedy American banks in uproar over promissory notes

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the preceding piece sits above the next
the banks of a word are its outside letters, here those of uproar

parts.note: IOUs, I owe you, are promissory notes

explanation.surface: American banks cause an uproar over unpaid debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like financial institutions, but it means the edges of uproar, U and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurious lending charges extortionate interest, so it means grasping or greedy.

indicators.note: round means the nurse's word goes around the little word

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse makes her rounds in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means menacing or dark in character.

clue.text: 'Howards End' is not broadly speaking extremely literary or very good

indicators.note: end refers to the last letter of the word Howards

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of is not

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters of literary

explanation.surface: A critic judges that Howards End is not really a great literary work.
explanation.walkthrough: Howards End is a novel by E. M. Forster; here 'End' just picks its title word's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly describes extreme goodness or virtue, like a saint.

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: The sound of a mysterious musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' suggests music, but it is a tool; YAWL is also a boat, a further false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: To yawl is an old dialect verb meaning to howl or cry out loudly.

clue.text: Pasta sauce and portion of extra guacamole

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ordering a sauce for pasta with an added side of guacamole.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragu is an Italian meat-based sauce served with pasta.

clue.text: Greek plonk in container without cap tipped over

indicators.note: tipped over in a down clue means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top
without cap means the top letter is removed

parts.note: a canister is a container

explanation.surface: Cheap Greek wine spilling from a toppled, lidless can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without cap' gives ANISTER from CANISTER; 'tipped over' turns that to RETSINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a resin-flavoured Greek white wine, often cheap, hence plonk.

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A women's rowing team makes an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight means influence or importance, the same sense as impact.

clue.text: Set out twice resolving to fly

indicators.note: twice says the rearranged piece is written two times
out suggests the letters of set are put out of order

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solver repeats setting out an answer to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SET into TSE, written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

indicators.note: report of means the sound of the referenced word as spoken

parts.note: the answer to 10 across is a word for an author

explanation.surface: A condiment is reported to the earlier answer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the word for author at 10 is heard as this Indian yoghurt dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yoghurt side dish served as a relish with Indian food.

clue.text: Banter from spectator either side of half-time

indicators.note: either side of means the spectator's word goes around the time fragment

parts.note: a witness is an onlooker or spectator

indicators.note: half picks the first two letters of time

explanation.surface: Jokes from a football fan at the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' looks like the football interval, but it means half of the word time; 'either side of' wraps the onlooker round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wittiness is clever humour, the quality of good banter.

clue.text: Italian football club trainee has name taken

indicators.note: taken means removed, so the name letter comes away

parts.note: an intern is a trainee

explanation.surface: An Italian football club signs a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: Inter Milan is a famous Italian football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter, short for Internazionale, is a leading Milan football club.

parts.note: out means out of fashion or unpopular
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An unwelcome moment to lose electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a period when electricity supply fails.

parts.note: an air is an appearance or look
tight means mean or stingy

explanation.surface: Someone appears stingy and closed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Airtight means sealed so nothing can get through, hence impenetrable.

indicators.note: mess means disorder, so the letters of direst are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting out of a dreadful situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step, a type of walking pace.

clue.text: Stranglers perform hits with this instrument

definitions.text: Stranglers perform hits with this instrument

parts.words: Stranglers perform hits with this instrument
parts.note: reads like the rock band The Stranglers playing hit songs on a musical instrument, but it is a killer's strangling device

explanation.surface: The punk band The Stranglers playing their hits on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stranglers are a British punk band; 'hits' are really murders.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotte is a wire or cord used for strangling.
